title: A law for Germany's children

facts.text: On 1 December 1936 Hitler and Hans Lammers, head of the Reich Chancellery, signed the Law on the Hitler Youth. Its first article said that all German youth within the Reich was organized in the Hitler Youth.
The law gave the Hitler Youth the job of raising the young, alongside home and school, physically, intellectually and morally in the spirit of National Socialism.
Baldur von Schirach, the Nazi party's youth leader, became Youth Leader of the German Reich. His office became a top Reich authority in Berlin, answering directly to Hitler.

The movement had grown fast under pressure and incentives: about 100,000 members in January 1933, more than 5 million by the end of 1936, and 5.4 million, about 65 percent of Germans aged 10 to 18, in 1937. Jewish children were barred.

The law itself named no penalty, and historians still argue over how far it made membership compulsory. A decree of March 1939, the Youth Service Ordinance, made service a legal duty for all young Germans aged 10 to 18.
The Nuremberg tribunal found that by the time formal conscription came, 97 percent of those eligible were already members.
Schirach left the youth post in 1940 to become Gauleiter of Vienna, where he took part in the deportation of the city's remaining Jews. He was replaced by Artur Axmann, 27.

Boys raised in the movement went to war. In 1943 the Waffen SS formed a division from Hitler Youth members born in 1926, aged 16 and 17; it fought in Normandy and the Ardennes and took part in massacres in France.

In the last months the Volkssturm militia called up males from 16 to 60, many of them Hitler Youth. In March 1945, 16 year old Willi Hübner was decorated with the Iron Cross after the fighting for Lauban in Silesia. Thousands of boys fought and died even as defeat became certain.
At Nuremberg on 24 May 1946 Schirach told the court: "The guilt is mine in that I educated the youth of Germany for a man who murdered by the millions."

On 1 October 1946 the tribunal acquitted him of crimes against peace but convicted him of crimes against humanity for his part in the Vienna deportations. He served his full 20 years in Spandau, was released on 1 October 1966, and died in 1974.

photoNote: Tier: green. Two uniformed boys in Worms stand with their bicycles carrying hand lettered recruiting signs for the Jungvolk, the Hitler Youth branch for boys aged 10 to 14 ("Bist du ein deutscher Junge? Dann hinein ins Jung-Volk!" and "Hinein ins Jungvolk"). Bundesarchiv Bild 133-131 (Gaubildarchiv Worms), photographer not named (o.Ang.), dated 1933 on Commons and 1933/1939 ca. on the print border; CC BY-SA 3.0 de. NOT a photo of 1 December 1936: it shows the membership drive the law was written to push. Commons original is 800 x 536; saved 960 x 643 from the Commons 960 px thumbnail (upscaled, soft at full size), the Bundesarchiv border strip with the number is visible at the bottom and can be cropped. Chosen for faces and for the story: children recruiting children, with no swastika or regalia in focus. Runner up: Bundesarchiv Bild 146-1979-099-01A, Heimabend der H.J. (an indoctrination evening, fits the film's classroom theme).
photoCredit: Hitler Youth boys with Jungvolk recruiting signs, Worms, about 1933. Bundesarchiv, Bild 133-131, photographer unknown, CC BY-SA 3.0.

videoPhotos.credit: A Hitler Youth home evening. Bundesarchiv, Bild 146-1979-099-01A, CC BY-SA 3.0.
Hitler Youth rifle training. Bundesarchiv, Bild 146-1978-013-27, photographer Hamann, CC BY-SA 3.0.
Hitler Youth boys wounded as helpers during air raids. Bundesarchiv, Bild 183-J08403, CC BY-SA 3.0 (check date and caption on the file page).

16 year old Willi Hübner decorated with the Iron Cross after the fighting for Lauban, March 1945. Bundesarchiv, Bild 183-G0627-500-001, CC BY-SA 3.0. Propaganda photo; Artur Axmann is in it, so frame the boy, never the leaders.

declassified.fact: The 1936 law was also about money. A 2024 study finds that Nazi leaders worded its second article to press towns and districts into paying for thousands of new Hitler Youth homes, and kept pushing municipalities to fund them into the war years.

film.record: Prelude to War (1942, U.S. War Department, Why We Fight 1), 111-OF-1 reel 3 (NARA 36067)
film.license: U.S. government film; the German film inside it is usable with a caption under Brian's 13 Nov 2026 rule (German film inside a U.S. government film). Italian and Japanese film inside it stays out.
film.shot_notes: First 4 minutes of reel 3 (the research cut; the full reel is 343 MB). Narration and score throughout; run silent (never keep German song or speech). 1 P.M. (Tuesday Lunch Drop video, this card): 00:45 to 01:12, Hitler Youth and BDM girls in rows at a rally, a drummer boy close up (01:00), a line of drums (01:05 to 01:12); open on the drummer at 01:00. Also German: 00:10 to 00:44 the Nazi classroom, children reciting, a teacher at a blackboard with burned in English subtitles from the U.S. film ("Adolf Hitler is our savior, our hero"); 02:03 to 02:12 a Hitler Youth fife player. AVOID: 01:13 to 01:24 Japanese children (out), 01:25 to 02:02 and 02:15 to 02:29 Italian youth (Italian film is never used), 02:14 a Japanese flag. 02:30 onward adult parades. No swastika banner as the opening frame.
film.date_note: German film of the Hitler Youth from the 1930s inside the U.S. film Prelude to War (1942), not dated to 1 Dec 1936. Caption: German film, from the U.S. Army's Prelude to War (1942); picture only, never presented as fact.

video.note: Prelude to War (1942), 111-OF-1 reel 3 (NARA 36067), German film of the Hitler Youth inside the U.S. film, run silent (narration and score). Cut 26 Nov 2026 (evening run): 00:59.6 to 01:02.9 a drum struck close, then a drummer boy (opening); 01:03.0 to 01:05.25 a boy playing a horn; 01:06.0 to 01:09.25 the drum line marching; 01:10.0 to 01:13.25 massed drummers; 02:10.3 to 02:13.3 a fife player. Left out 00:48.5 to 00:59.5, which shows a rising sun flag and banners in Japanese (Japanese youth, not German, though research's notes put the Hitler Youth there), the flag at 01:05.5, the Japanese children from 01:13.5, the Italian youth, the quotation card at 02:02, and the swastika banners at 02:07 to 02:10. Pillarbox cropped, scaled to 640 x 480.
